findings.problem: The proof characterising the normal space as the orthogonal complement of the velocity manually unfolds mem_normalSubspace_iff, introduces an auxiliary linear map D, and extracts a multiple in each direction. Given hrange : range D = ℝ ∙ deriv (f ∘ Circle.exp) t, the two Submodule.mem_span_singleton extractions and the D binding are unnecessary machinery for the single mathematical fact normalSpace = (ℝ ∙ velocity)ᗮ.

This rewrites the normal space using its @[expose] definition and the range identity hrange, then closes by the named orthogonal-complement-of-a-singleton lemma.
findings.benefit: The reader sees the chain normal space = (range of mfderiv)ᗮ = (ℝ ∙ velocity)ᵍ = {v | ⟪velocity, v⟫ = 0} directly. The named lemma inside Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right states the final equality exactly, so the manual scalar extraction no longer hides the mathematical idea.
